title: The Midnight Library
author: Matt Haig
description: Between life and death, Nora Seed finds a library of lives she could have lived. Every book offers another beginning, and a new way to understand the life she already has.

title: Atomic Habits
author: James Clear
description: Small changes can become remarkable results when repeated with intention. Explore practical ways to build better routines, design a helpful environment, and make progress one ordinary day at a time.

title: The Alchemist
author: Paulo Coelho
description: A young shepherd follows a recurring dream beyond the familiar hills of Spain. His journey across the desert becomes a quiet exploration of purpose, courage, and listening to the world.

title: The Little Prince
author: Antoine de Saint-Exupéry
description: A pilot stranded in the desert meets a visitor from a tiny planet. Their conversations explore friendship, responsibility, and the things that matter beyond appearances.

title: The Hobbit
author: J. R. R. Tolkien
description: Bilbo Baggins leaves his comfortable home with a company of dwarves. An unlikely adventure reveals resources of courage he never expected to possess.

title: Pride and Prejudice
author: Jane Austen
description: Elizabeth Bennet values wit and independence more than social rank. An unexpected connection challenges her first impressions of the reserved Mr. Darcy.

title: The Thursday Murder Club
author: Richard Osman
description: Four residents of a retirement village enjoy discussing unsolved crimes. A nearby death gives their informal club a very current case.

title: The Psychology of Money
author: Morgan Housel
description: Short essays explore the behavior behind financial decisions. Patience, uncertainty, and personal experience receive more attention than complex formulas.

title: Dune
author: Frank Herbert
description: A young heir arrives on a desert planet whose rare resource holds an empire together. Politics, ecology, and prophecy converge around a contested future.

title: A Man Called Ove
author: Fredrik Backman
description: A solitary man's carefully ordered routine is interrupted by new neighbors. Unexpected friendships begin to reveal the tenderness behind his stubborn exterior.

title: Book Lovers
author: Emily Henry
description: A literary agent reluctantly takes a small-town holiday with her sister. An editor she knows from work keeps appearing in the least convenient places.

title: Devotions
author: Mary Oliver
description: A selection gathers poems from across Mary Oliver's career. Close attention to the natural world opens onto questions of gratitude and belonging.

title: The Great Gatsby
author: F. Scott Fitzgerald
description: A mysterious millionaire fills his Long Island home with dazzling parties. Beneath the glamour, a story of longing, reinvention, and the American dream unfolds.

title: To Kill a Mockingbird
author: Harper Lee
description: Through a child's eyes, a small Southern town reveals its kindness and its prejudice. Scout Finch watches her father defend his principles in an unequal world.

author: George Orwell
description: Winston Smith lives in a society where the government watches every move. His search for private truth becomes a dangerous act of resistance.

title: Jane Eyre
author: Charlotte Brontë
description: An orphan becomes a governess at an isolated English house. Jane must balance her growing affection with a fierce commitment to her own dignity.

title: Little Women
author: Louisa May Alcott
description: Four sisters grow up with different talents and shared ambitions. Family, creativity, and everyday courage shape their paths into adulthood.

title: Wuthering Heights
author: Emily Brontë
description: Two families on the Yorkshire moors become bound by an intense attachment. A visitor gradually uncovers the consequences of pride and revenge.

title: The Picture of Dorian Gray
author: Oscar Wilde
description: A young man wishes his portrait could age in his place. The strange bargain exposes the distance between outward beauty and an unexamined life.

title: Frankenstein
author: Mary Shelley
description: A scientist brings a new being into existence and abandons it. Creator and creation confront the consequences of ambition without responsibility.

title: Dracula
author: Bram Stoker
description: Letters and diaries trace a disturbing arrival in Victorian England. A small group joins forces against a threat that crosses the border between life and death.

title: The Count of Monte Cristo
author: Alexandre Dumas
description: Wrongfully imprisoned, Edmond Dantès discovers a chance to begin again. His elaborate return tests the difference between justice and revenge.

title: Adventures of Huckleberry Finn
author: Mark Twain
description: Huck and Jim travel down the Mississippi River on a raft. Their encounters raise questions about freedom, friendship, and the rules society accepts.

title: Great Expectations
author: Charles Dickens
description: An unexpected fortune changes the life of a young apprentice. Pip discovers that becoming a gentleman is not the same as becoming a good person.

title: Anna Karenina
author: Leo Tolstoy
description: The lives of two families unfold across Russian society. Love, duty, and the search for meaning pull their members in different directions.

title: The Kite Runner
author: Khaled Hosseini
description: A childhood friendship in Kabul leaves an adult man with unfinished questions. A return journey offers a difficult chance to face the past.

title: A Thousand Splendid Suns
author: Khaled Hosseini
description: Two women from different generations find their lives joined in Afghanistan. Their growing bond becomes a source of courage through years of upheaval.

title: The Book Thief
author: Markus Zusak
description: A young girl in wartime Germany finds refuge in stolen books and shared words. Her foster family teaches her that small acts of kindness can carry enormous weight.

title: The Night Circus
author: Erin Morgenstern
description: A black-and-white circus appears without warning and opens only at night. Two young performers discover that their work is part of a much larger contest.

title: The Secret History
author: Donna Tartt
description: A student joins an exclusive group studying ancient Greek at a small college. Their intellectual fascination slowly gives way to a dangerous separation from ordinary life.

title: Normal People
author: Sally Rooney
description: Connell and Marianne move between connection and distance from school to university. Their changing circumstances expose the difficulty of saying what they need.

title: The Goldfinch
author: Donna Tartt
description: After a sudden tragedy, a boy carries away a small painting. The artwork becomes an enduring link between grief, beauty, and the choices that shape his adulthood.

title: Tomorrow, and Tomorrow, and Tomorrow
author: Gabrielle Zevin
description: Two childhood friends reunite to make video games together. Creative partnership brings extraordinary possibilities alongside the ordinary complications of being human.

title: Eleanor Oliphant Is Completely Fine
author: Gail Honeyman
description: A woman follows a very precise weekly routine with little room for other people. An unexpected act of kindness starts to open a different kind of life.

title: The Remains of the Day
author: Kazuo Ishiguro
description: An English butler looks back on decades of service during a short road trip. His memories reveal the personal cost of loyalty and emotional restraint.

title: Never Let Me Go
author: Kazuo Ishiguro
description: Three friends remember their time at a secluded English school. As their shared future becomes clearer, familiar memories take on an unsettling meaning.

title: Pachinko
author: Min Jin Lee
description: Four generations of a Korean family build lives in Japan. Their story follows the work, sacrifice, and resilience behind a search for belonging.

title: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone
author: J. K. Rowling
description: An ordinary-looking boy discovers a hidden magical world. His first year at a school of witchcraft brings friendship, puzzles, and an unexpected inheritance.

title: The Name of the Wind
author: Patrick Rothfuss
description: An innkeeper begins telling the story behind his many legends. Music, learning, and loss shape the early life of a gifted young traveler.

title: A Wizard of Earthsea
author: Ursula K. Le Guin
description: A talented young wizard releases a shadow through his own pride. His journey across an island world becomes a lesson in balance and self-knowledge.

title: The Fellowship of the Ring
author: J. R. R. Tolkien
description: A quiet hobbit inherits an object that threatens the whole of Middle-earth. A fellowship forms to carry it beyond the reach of its former master.

title: The Two Towers
author: J. R. R. Tolkien
description: The fellowship separates as war spreads across Middle-earth. Different paths test the loyalty and endurance of its members.

title: The Return of the King
author: J. R. R. Tolkien
description: The struggle for Middle-earth reaches its final turning point. Great armies and two small travelers must each finish what they began.

title: Good Omens
author: Terry Pratchett & Neil Gaiman
description: An angel and a demon have grown rather attached to life on Earth. An approaching apocalypse persuades these unlikely friends to work together.

title: Stardust
author: Neil Gaiman
description: A young man crosses a guarded wall to retrieve a fallen star. Beyond his village, a simple promise becomes an adventure through a stranger country.

title: Howl's Moving Castle
author: Diana Wynne Jones
description: A young hatmaker is transformed by a witch's spell. She seeks help in a wandering castle inhabited by an unreliable wizard and a fire demon.

title: The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe
author: C. S. Lewis
description: Four siblings step through a wardrobe into a snow-covered land. Their arrival offers hope to a world caught in an unnaturally long winter.

title: The Ocean at the End of the Lane
author: Neil Gaiman
description: A return to a childhood home awakens memories of a remarkable neighboring family. The familiar countryside opens onto a much older and stranger world.

title: Piranesi
author: Susanna Clarke
description: A man lives among endless halls, statues, and rising tides. His careful observations slowly challenge everything he understands about his home.

title: The Last Unicorn
author: Peter S. Beagle
description: A unicorn leaves her forest to discover what happened to the rest of her kind. Two unlikely companions join a journey about wonder and change.

title: The Fifth Season
author: N. K. Jemisin
description: In a land repeatedly broken by geological catastrophe, some people can control the earth. Three connected stories reveal the human cost of this power.

title: The Hound of the Baskervilles
author: Arthur Conan Doyle
description: A family legend casts a shadow over an isolated estate. Sherlock Holmes and Dr. Watson investigate the very real danger behind an apparently supernatural threat.

title: Murder on the Orient Express
author: Agatha Christie
description: A luxury train is stranded in deep snow after a passenger is killed. Hercule Poirot studies a carriage full of travelers with carefully guarded stories.

title: And Then There Were None
author: Agatha Christie
description: Ten strangers arrive on a remote island at an absent host's invitation. A disturbing message reveals that each has been chosen for a reason.

title: The Murder of Roger Ackroyd
author: Agatha Christie
description: A village death brings Hercule Poirot out of retirement. A local doctor's account follows the clues behind an unusually complicated household.

title: The Big Sleep
author: Raymond Chandler
description: Private investigator Philip Marlowe accepts a case from a wealthy family. Blackmail leads him through a Los Angeles where almost everyone has something to hide.

title: The Maltese Falcon
author: Dashiell Hammett
description: Sam Spade becomes involved in a search for a valuable statuette. Conflicting stories and shifting loyalties make every new client difficult to trust.

title: Rebecca
author: Daphne du Maurier
description: A young bride enters a grand house still shaped by its former mistress. The memory of Rebecca seems to occupy every room and conversation.

title: The Moonstone
author: Wilkie Collins
description: A valuable diamond disappears from an English country house. Different narrators offer pieces of a puzzle built from family secrets and mistaken assumptions.

title: The Woman in White
author: Wilkie Collins
description: A drawing teacher encounters a distressed woman on a moonlit road. Her appearance draws him into a mystery of identity, inheritance, and confinement.

title: Gone Girl
author: Gillian Flynn
description: A woman's disappearance turns a marriage into a public investigation. Alternating accounts expose how differently two people can tell the same story.

title: The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo
author: Stieg Larsson
description: A journalist and a gifted researcher revisit a decades-old disappearance. Their investigation uncovers the hidden history of a powerful family.

title: The Silent Patient
author: Alex Michaelides
description: A painter stops speaking after a violent event. A psychotherapist becomes determined to understand the story behind her silence.

title: In the Woods
author: Tana French
description: A detective returns to a town linked to a mystery from his own childhood. A new case tests the boundary between professional judgment and personal memory.

title: The No. 1 Ladies' Detective Agency
author: Alexander McCall Smith
description: Precious Ramotswe opens a detective agency in Botswana. Patience, observation, and a deep understanding of people guide her first investigations.

title: Beach Read
author: Emily Henry
description: Two writers with very different approaches become summer neighbors. A creative challenge encourages each to try telling a different kind of story.

title: People We Meet on Vacation
author: Emily Henry
description: Two friends have spent years taking one holiday together each summer. A final trip may give them a chance to address the distance between them.

title: The Love Hypothesis
author: Ali Hazelwood
description: A graduate student begins a pretend relationship to help a friend. The arrangement becomes harder to explain when genuine feelings complicate her carefully reasoned plan.

title: The Flatshare
author: Beth O'Leary
description: Two people share a London flat while working opposite shifts. Notes left around their home create a friendship before they properly meet.

title: Red, White & Royal Blue
author: Casey McQuiston
description: A public misunderstanding brings an American first son and a British prince together. A carefully managed friendship develops beyond the limits of their official roles.

title: The Hating Game
author: Sally Thorne
description: Two publishing assistants turn office life into a series of competitions. A promotion forces them to reconsider what really lies behind their rivalry.

title: The Kiss Quotient
author: Helen Hoang
description: A successful econometrician approaches dating as a problem she can study. The person she asks to help challenges her expectations about compatibility.

title: The Rosie Project
author: Graeme Simsion
description: A genetics professor designs a questionnaire to find a suitable partner. An unexpected visitor offers a different and less predictable kind of project.

title: The Time Traveler's Wife
author: Audrey Niffenegger
description: An artist builds a life with a man who moves unpredictably through time. Their relationship asks what commitment means when chronology cannot be relied upon.

title: One Day
author: David Nicholls
description: Two graduates spend a night together before their adult lives begin. The story revisits the same date over many years of friendship and change.

title: Me Before You
author: Jojo Moyes
description: A young woman accepts a job caring for a man whose life has changed after an accident. Their meeting challenges the limits each has placed on the future.

title: The Notebook
author: Nicholas Sparks
description: An older man reads a love story from a notebook to a fellow resident. The account follows two young people whose lives repeatedly take them apart.

title: Persuasion
author: Jane Austen
description: Anne Elliot encounters the man she was persuaded not to marry years earlier. Changed circumstances offer a quiet examination of regret and second chances.

title: Emma
author: Jane Austen
description: A confident young woman enjoys arranging the romantic lives of her neighbors. Her matchmaking reveals how little she understands about her own feelings.

title: The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy
author: Douglas Adams
description: Arthur Dent escapes Earth just before its demolition. A very unusual guidebook helps him navigate the absurdities of a much larger universe.

title: The Martian
author: Andy Weir
description: An astronaut is accidentally left alone on Mars. Practical problem-solving becomes a daily struggle to survive until help can reach him.

title: Project Hail Mary
author: Andy Weir
description: A man awakens on a spacecraft without knowing his mission. Recovering his memory is only the first step toward solving a problem that threatens his home.

title: Foundation
author: Isaac Asimov
description: A mathematician predicts the decline of a galactic empire. A small group tries to preserve knowledge through the long period of uncertainty ahead.

title: I, Robot
author: Isaac Asimov
description: Interlinked stories examine the behavior of intelligent machines. Apparently simple rules produce complicated questions about logic and responsibility.

title: The Left Hand of Darkness
author: Ursula K. Le Guin
description: An envoy arrives on a world with unfamiliar social and biological customs. A journey across a frozen landscape gradually builds a difficult trust.

title: The Dispossessed
author: Ursula K. Le Guin
description: A physicist travels between two neighboring societies organized around different ideals. His work challenges the boundaries that keep their inhabitants apart.

title: A Wrinkle in Time
author: Madeleine L'Engle
description: Three children travel across space in search of a missing scientist. Their adventure connects questions of family, difference, and personal courage.

title: Ender's Game
author: Orson Scott Card
description: A gifted child enters an orbital school designed to train military commanders. Strategy games gradually raise unsettling questions about the purpose of his education.

title: The War of the Worlds
author: H. G. Wells
description: Strange cylinders arrive in the English countryside carrying invaders from Mars. An ordinary observer describes a civilization abruptly stripped of its confidence.

title: The Time Machine
author: H. G. Wells
description: An inventor travels into a distant future that seems peaceful at first. His discoveries suggest a more troubling history beneath the surface.

title: Fahrenheit 451
author: Ray Bradbury
description: A fireman's job is to burn books rather than save buildings. A series of encounters makes him question the society he helps maintain.

title: Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep?
author: Philip K. Dick
description: A bounty hunter tracks artificial humans on a damaged Earth. The work complicates his understanding of empathy and the boundary of personhood.

title: The Three-Body Problem
author: Liu Cixin
description: A scientific mystery connects a turbulent past with a possible extraterrestrial future. Researchers confront a problem whose consequences extend far beyond Earth.

title: Sapiens
author: Yuval Noah Harari
description: A broad account follows human societies from early foraging communities to the modern world. Shared stories and collective institutions provide the connecting thread.

title: Educated
author: Tara Westover
description: A memoir traces one woman's journey from an isolated upbringing to formal education. Learning creates new possibilities while complicating her connection to family.

title: Becoming
author: Michelle Obama
description: Michelle Obama reflects on her childhood, professional life, and years in the White House. Personal recollections explore how identity develops through changing public roles.

title: Man's Search for Meaning
author: Viktor E. Frankl
description: A psychiatrist reflects on survival and the human search for purpose. Personal experience provides the starting point for an approach to finding meaning in difficult circumstances.

title: The Power of Habit
author: Charles Duhigg
description: Stories from everyday life and organizations examine how habits take shape. Understanding the cue, routine, and reward offers a way to reconsider familiar patterns.

title: Deep Work
author: Cal Newport
description: Focused attention can be difficult to protect in a distracted environment. This book explores habits and boundaries that support sustained, meaningful work.

title: Quiet
author: Susan Cain
description: An exploration of introversion questions the assumption that confidence must be loud. Research and personal stories consider different ways to contribute and connect.

title: Thinking, Fast and Slow
author: Daniel Kahneman
description: A psychologist examines the shortcuts and deliberation behind everyday decisions. Familiar examples reveal how judgment can be both useful and predictably mistaken.

title: A Brief History of Time
author: Stephen Hawking
description: An introduction to cosmology considers time, black holes, and the beginnings of the universe. Large scientific questions are presented for a general audience.

title: Into the Wild
author: Jon Krakauer
description: A journalist investigates the journey of a young traveler who sought life outside familiar expectations. Interviews and documents reveal competing interpretations of his choices.

title: When Breath Becomes Air
author: Paul Kalanithi
description: A neurosurgeon reflects on becoming a patient after a serious diagnosis. His memoir considers the relationship between meaningful work and a meaningful life.

title: Braiding Sweetgrass
author: Robin Wall Kimmerer
description: A botanist brings scientific training into conversation with Indigenous knowledge. Essays about plants and place explore reciprocity and responsibility to the living world.

title: The Art of War
author: Sun Tzu
description: A concise collection considers strategy, preparation, and understanding circumstances. Its reflections on conflict invite careful reading beyond a literal battlefield.

title: The Prophet
author: Kahlil Gibran
description: A traveler preparing to leave a city answers questions from its inhabitants. Lyrical reflections explore love, work, friendship, and the rhythms of a human life.

title: Leaves of Grass
author: Walt Whitman
description: An expansive collection celebrates bodies, landscapes, and the varied lives of ordinary people. Its free verse seeks connections between individual experience and a shared world.

title: Milk and Honey
author: Rupi Kaur
description: Short poems and spare illustrations move through hurt, healing, and self-discovery. Four sections organize the collection around stages of emotional change.

title: The Sun and Her Flowers
author: Rupi Kaur
description: A collection follows an arc from loss toward renewal. Family, migration, and personal growth recur through accessible poems and accompanying drawings.

title: A Thousand Mornings
author: Mary Oliver
description: Everyday encounters with birds, light, and changing seasons become occasions for reflection. These poems find unexpected depth in the practice of noticing.

title: The Waste Land
author: T. S. Eliot
description: Fragmented voices and literary echoes form a portrait of cultural dislocation. A modernist poem invites readers to follow connections across shifting scenes and languages.

title: The Essential Rumi
author: Rumi
description: A translated selection introduces the imagery and spiritual questions associated with Rumi. Everyday objects become starting points for reflections on love and transformation.

title: Twenty Love Poems and a Song of Despair
author: Pablo Neruda
description: A sequence of poems explores the changing intensity of young love. Landscapes and sensory images express both closeness and the experience of absence.

title: Ariel
author: Sylvia Plath
description: Vivid images and tightly controlled language animate this influential collection. The poems confront questions of voice, identity, and personal transformation.

title: The Collected Poems of Emily Dickinson
author: Emily Dickinson
description: Compact poems turn familiar subjects into unsettling questions. Slant rhyme, dashes, and startling images explore nature, belief, and the limits of certainty.

title: Citizen: An American Lyric
author: Claudia Rankine
description: Poetry, prose, and visual material examine everyday experiences of racism. The collection asks readers to consider the cumulative force of ordinary encounters.

title: The Wild Iris
author: Louise Glück
description: Voices move through a garden across a growing season. Human questions and the lives of flowers meet in poems about change, vulnerability, and renewal.

title: Night Sky with Exit Wounds
author: Ocean Vuong
description: A debut collection brings family history into conversation with migration and memory. Intimate images examine the ways language can hold both loss and possibility.

title: The Carrying
author: Ada Limón
description: These poems pay close attention to bodies, animals, and everyday landscapes. Questions of belonging and resilience emerge from the texture of ordinary days.
